children: Wall Street retreated Wednesday as Treasury yields surged, adding pressure to equities even as investors weighed signs of potential U.S.-Iran negotiations.

said the decline followed the Nasdaq’s record high on Tuesday, but argued that the pullback reflected more than profit-taking. “The euphoria eventually has to ease,” Jones stated, while pointing to mounting concerns over monetary policy and the bond market.
On Wednesday the Dow Jones Industrial Average

The 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since mid-2007, while Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said further rate adjustments may be necessary to maintain price stability. A weaker-than-expected five-year Treasury auction added to pressure in the bond market.
Jones also cited elevated oil prices and uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict.
“When you add on top of this the fact that oil prices remain high,” he said, “you can understand why this downward pressure developed.”
He expects economic conditions to deteriorate further, warning of a potential stagflationary recession. Jones said investors should prepare for more downward pressure in coming weeks ahead.
